- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history; model reacts too aggressively, peaking too soon.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of forecast, suggesting mean reversion or downward momentum not captured.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in downward trends.
- High variance in forecast errors during periods of low volatility; model overfits to recent high volatility.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or cyclical patterns in the 30-day history, especially around mid-forecast horizon.
- When history shows a clear downward trend, model often fails to recognize it and continues upward bias.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in the 15–25 day window; model underestimates downward corrections in this range.
